claim: TG6 TCR transgenic mice exhibit strong skewing to the CD8 lineage even in a Rag2-sufficient background.
source: Mice expressing rearranged TCR α and β transgenes from a T cell clone (TG6) with low self-reactivity exhibit a strong skewing to the CD8 lineage even in a Rag2-sufficient background (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation directly and references Figure 1—figure supplement 1 as supporting data.

claim: TG6 mice show robust positive selection in contrast with the HY TCR transgenic model.
source: This is indicative of robust positive selection and is in contrast with the HY TCR transgenic model where low self-reactivity is accompanied by extensive endogenous receptor rearrangement and weak skewing to the CD8 lineage (Azzam et al., 2001; Kisielow et al., 1988).
evidence: The manuscript compares TG6 to HY TCR transgenic model and cites previous studies.

claim: CD8SP thymocytes from TG6 mice express low levels of CD5 compared to wild-type mice.
source: Compared to CD8SP from wild-type mice, CD8SP thymocytes from TG6 mice express low levels of CD5, a reliable surface marker of T cell self-reactivity (Figure 1a,b; Azzam et al., 1998; Mandl et al., 2013; Fulton et al., 2015; Persaud et al., 2014; Azzam et al., 2001).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 1a,b and cites multiple studies establishing CD5 as a marker of self-reactivity.

claim: CD5 is a reliable surface marker of T cell self-reactivity.
source: Compared to CD8SP from wild-type mice, CD8SP thymocytes from TG6 mice express low levels of CD5, a reliable surface marker of T cell self-reactivity (Figure 1a,b; Azzam et al., 1998; Mandl et al., 2013; Fulton et al., 2015; Persaud et al., 2014; Azzam et al., 2001).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge and cites multiple supporting studies.

claim: CD8SP thymocytes from TG6 mice have relatively low expression of Nur77.
source: CD8SP thymocytes from TG6 mice also have relatively low expression of Nur77, a marker of recent TCR signaling that also correlates with self-reactivity (Figure 1c; Fulton et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 1c and cites a study.

claim: Nur77 is a marker of recent TCR signaling that correlates with self-reactivity.
source: CD8SP thymocytes from TG6 mice also have relatively low expression of Nur77, a marker of recent TCR signaling that also correlates with self-reactivity (Figure 1c; Fulton et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge and cites a supporting study.

claim: CD8SP from OT-1 and F5 TCR transgenic models have high and intermediate levels of CD5 and Nur77, respectively.
source: In contrast, CD8SP from two well-characterized TCRtg models, OT-1 and F5, have high and intermediate levels of these markers, respectively (Figure 1a–c; Fulton et al., 2015; Cho et al., 2016; Dong et al., 2017; Kieper et al., 2004; Palmer et al., 2011; Ge et al., 2004).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 1a-c and cites multiple studies.

claim: The relative levels of CD5 and Nur77 in TCRtg lymph node T cells follow a similar pattern to thymic cells, except that Nur77 expression in F5 T cells decreases in lymph node relative to thymus.
source: The relative levels of CD5 and Nur77 in TCRtg lymph node T cells follow a similar pattern, except that expression of Nur77 in F5 T cells decreases somewhat in lymph node relative to thymus (Figure 1d).
evidence: The manuscript presents this observation with reference to Figure 1d.

claim: The decrease in Nur77 expression in F5 T cells in the periphery may reflect weaker recognition of peripheral versus thymic self-peptides by F5.
source: This may reflect weaker recognition of peripheral versus thymic self-peptides by F5, and the loss of β5t-derived peptides in the periphery, in line with the β5t-dependence of F5 thymocytes Nitta et al., 2010.
evidence: The manuscript speculates on the mechanism and cites a study.

claim: TG6, F5, and OT-1 TCR transgenic models span the range of self-reactivity for CD8 T cell-positive selection.
source: Thus, these three TCRtg models span the range of self-reactivity for CD8 T cell-positive selection, with TG6 providing an example of low self-reactivity coupled with relatively efficient positive selection.
evidence: The manuscript concludes this based on the CD5 and Nur77 data presented.

claim: OT-1 thymocytes undergoing positive selection exhibit serial TCR signals lasting about 4 minutes and associated with a migratory pause.
source: Previous time-lapse studies of OT-1 thymocytes undergoing positive selection in situ revealed serial TCR signals lasting about 4 min and associated with a migratory pause (Ross et al., 2014; Melichar et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies that reported this finding.

claim: For both TG6 and OT-1, the frequency of time points with elevated calcium was greater on selecting compared to nonselecting thymic slices.
source: For both TG6 and OT-1, the frequency of time points with elevated calcium was greater on selecting, compared to nonselecting thymic slices (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Calcium flux under these experimental conditions is dependent on the presence of positive selecting ligands.
source: This confirmed that calcium flux under these conditions is dependent on the presence of positive selecting ligands.
evidence: The manuscript infers this from the difference in calcium flux between selecting and nonselecting slices.

claim: TG6 cells in positively selecting slices spent slightly less time signaling than did OT-1 cells, although the difference did not reach statistical significance.
source: In line with their lower self-reactivity, TG6 cells in positively selecting slices spent slightly less time signaling than did OT-1 cells, although the difference did not reach statistical significance (Figure 2b, Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to figures and supplementary file.

claim: At both 3 and 6 hours after addition to the slice, the average signaling event for TG6 thymocytes is about one minute shorter than OT-1.
source: At both 3 and 6 hr after addition to the slice, the average signaling event for TG6 thymocytes is about one minute shorter than OT-1 (Figure 2c,d; Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 2c,d and videos.

claim: OT-1 thymocytes pause during signaling events, as reflected in a decrease in the average speed of signaling portion of the track compared to nonsignaling portion.
source: Moreover, while OT-1 thymocytes pause during signaling events, as reflected in a decrease in the average speed of signaling portion of the track compared to nonsignaling portion of the same cell track, TG6 thymocytes exhibit a less pronounced signal-associated pause at 3 hr, and no significant pause at the 6 hr time point (Figure 2e, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 2e and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: TG6 thymocytes exhibit a less pronounced signal-associated pause at 3 hours and no significant pause at 6 hours.
source: Moreover, while OT-1 thymocytes pause during signaling events, as reflected in a decrease in the average speed of signaling portion of the track compared to nonsignaling portion of the same cell track, TG6 thymocytes exhibit a less pronounced signal-associated pause at 3 hr, and no significant pause at the 6 hr time point (Figure 2e, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 2e and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The pause index was significantly higher for OT-1 than for TG6 at both 3 and 6 hours.
source: The pause index was significantly higher for OT-1 than for TG6 at both 3 and 6 hr (Figure 2f).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 2f.

claim: The frequency of signaling events for TG6 thymocytes was approximately half that for OT-1 thymocytes (one signaling event every 2 hours for TG6 versus one signaling event every 75 minutes for OT-1).
source: In addition, the frequency of signaling events for TG6 thymocytes was approximately half that for OT-1 thymocytes (one signaling event every 2 hr for TG6 thymocytes versus one signaling event every 75 min for OT-1: Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Supplementary file 2.

claim: Low self-reactivity is associated with less pronounced TCR-induced pausing and a reduction in both the duration and frequency of TCR signals during positive selection.
source: Thus, low self-reactivity is associated with less pronounced TCR-induced pausing and a reduction in both the duration and frequency of TCR signals during positive selection.
evidence: The manuscript concludes this based on the imaging data comparing TG6 and OT-1.

claim: Briefer TCR signals observed in TG6 thymocytes could mean that thymocytes with low self-reactivity need more time to accumulate sufficient signals to complete positive selection.
source: Briefer TCR signals observed in TG6 thymocytes could mean that thymocytes with low self-reactivity need more time to accumulate sufficient signals to complete positive selection (Au-Yeung et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript speculates on the implication of briefer TCR signals and cites a study.

claim: MHC-I-specific preselection DP thymocytes undergo a synchronous wave of maturation after introduction into positive selecting thymic tissue slices.
source: We previously showed that MHC-I-specific preselection DP thymocytes undergo a synchronous wave of maturation after introduction into positive selecting thymic tissue slices.
evidence: The manuscript refers to their previous work.

claim: Positive selection includes transient upregulation of CD69, followed by a switch in chemokine receptor expression from cortical (CXCR4) to medullary (CCR7) in DP thymocytes, and eventually CD4 downregulation.
source: This includes transient upregulation of the TCR activation marker CD69, followed by a switch in chemokine receptor expression from cortical (CXCR4) to medullary (CCR7) in DP thymocytes, and eventually CD4 downregulation (Ross et al., 2014; Melichar et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript describes the process and cites previous studies.

claim: Slice-developed TG6, F5, or OT-1 CD8SPs exhibit the same relative CD5 levels as their in vivo counterparts.
source: Slice-developed TG6, F5, or OT-1 CD8SPs exhibit the same relative CD5 levels as their in vivo counterparts (Figure 3a), indicating that thymic slices culture provide a good model for examining the impact of self-reactivity on positive selection.
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 3a.

claim: Thymic slice culture provides a good model for examining the impact of self-reactivity on positive selection.
source: Slice-developed TG6, F5, or OT-1 CD8SPs exhibit the same relative CD5 levels as their in vivo counterparts (Figure 3a), indicating that thymic slices culture provide a good model for examining the impact of self-reactivity on positive selection.
evidence: The manuscript infers this from the CD5 data.

claim: In all three TCR transgenic models, thymocytes exhibited a transient increase in CD69 expression; however, cells with lower self-reactivity reached peak CD69 expression later than cells with higher self-reactivity.
source: In all three models, thymocytes exhibited a transient increase in CD69 expression; however, cells with lower self-reactivity reached peak CD69 expression later than cells with higher self-reactivity (Figure 3b).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 3b.

claim: The switch in cortical to medullary chemokine receptor expression (CXCR4−CCR7+) and the appearance of CD8SP were delayed in thymocytes with lower self-reactivity.
source: In addition, the switch in cortical to medullary chemokine receptor expression (CXCR4−CCR7+) and the appearance of CD8SP were delayed in thymocytes with lower self-reactivity (Figure 3c,d, Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to multiple figures.

claim: The timing of all three major landmarks during positive selection is inversely correlated with self-reactivity.
source: Thus, the timing of all three major landmarks during positive selection is inversely correlated with self-reactivity, implying that cells with lower self-reactivity progress more slowly through positive selection.
evidence: The manuscript concludes this based on the thymic slice data.

claim: Cells with lower self-reactivity progress more slowly through positive selection.
source: Thus, the timing of all three major landmarks during positive selection is inversely correlated with self-reactivity, implying that cells with lower self-reactivity progress more slowly through positive selection.
evidence: The manuscript infers this from the timing data.

claim: Mature CD8SP thymocytes appear around the end of gestation in mice and gradually accumulate after birth.
source: Mature CD8SP thymocytes appear around the end of gestation in mice and gradually accumulate after birth.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge.

claim: If thymocytes with low self-reactivity proceed more slowly through positive selection, they may also appear more slowly during the neonatal period.
source: If thymocytes with low self-reactivity proceed more slowly through positive selection, they may also appear more slowly during the neonatal period.
evidence: The manuscript presents this as a hypothesis to be tested.

claim: CD8SP thymocytes accumulate slowly with age in TG6 mice, with the percent of CD8SP remaining significantly below maximal adult levels at 21 days after birth.
source: Consistent with thymic slice data, CD8SP thymocytes accumulate slowly with age in TG6 mice, with the percent of CD8SP remaining significantly below maximal adult levels at 21 days after birth (Figure 4a and b).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 4a and b.

claim: In OT-1 mice, CD8SP thymocytes reach their maximal levels at 7 days after birth.
source: In contrast, in OT-1 mice, CD8SP thymocytes reach their maximal levels at 7 days after birth, and F5 mice show an intermediate rate of accumulation (Figure 4a and b).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 4a and b.

claim: F5 mice show an intermediate rate of CD8SP accumulation.
source: In contrast, in OT-1 mice, CD8SP thymocytes reach their maximal levels at 7 days after birth, and F5 mice show an intermediate rate of accumulation (Figure 4a and b).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 4a and b.

claim: TG6 mice were slowest to accumulate CXCR4-CCR7+ CD4+CD8+DP and CD8SP thymocytes.
source: In addition, TG6 mice were slowest to accumulate CXCR4-CCR7 + CD4+CD8+DP and CD8SP thymocytes (Figure 4c) and exhibited delayed appearance of CD8SP cells in the spleen (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: TG6 mice exhibited delayed appearance of CD8SP cells in the spleen.
source: In addition, TG6 mice were slowest to accumulate CXCR4-CCR7 + CD4+CD8+DP and CD8SP thymocytes (Figure 4c) and exhibited delayed appearance of CD8SP cells in the spleen (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The neonatal data are consistent with thymic slice culture results and provide in vivo confirmation that the time to complete positive selection correlates inversely with thymocyte self-reactivity.
source: These results are consistent with results from thymic slice cultures and provide in vivo confirmation that the time to complete positive selection correlates inversely with thymocyte self-reactivity.
evidence: The manuscript concludes this based on the neonatal data.

claim: In vivo EdU injection labels a cohort of thymocytes proliferating after a successful TCRβ chain rearrangement at the time of the injection.
source: In vivo EdU injection labels a cohort of thymocytes proliferating after a successful TCRβ chain rearrangement at the time of the injection, which then can be detected by flow cytometry, as they undergo positive selection in vivo (Figure 5a; Lucas et al., 1993).
evidence: The manuscript describes the method and cites a study.

claim: EdU incorporated equally into the thymocytes of all three TCR transgenic models.
source: EdU incorporated equally into the thymocytes of all three TCRtgs (Figure 5b).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 5b.

claim: For F5 thymocytes, EdU+ CD8 SP overtook the DPs at day 5 post-injection.
source: For F5 thymocytes, EdU + CD8 SP overtook the DPs 1 day earlier (day 5 p.i.), and EdU + CD8 SP OT-1 thymocytes accumulated even more quickly – by day 4 p.i. (Figure 5c).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 5c.

claim: EdU+ CD8 SP OT-1 thymocytes accumulated by day 4 post-injection.
source: For F5 thymocytes, EdU + CD8 SP overtook the DPs 1 day earlier (day 5 p.i.), and EdU + CD8 SP OT-1 thymocytes accumulated even more quickly – by day 4 p.i. (Figure 5c).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 5c.

claim: The percentage of EdU+ CD8 SP thymocytes in OT-1 and F5 samples exhibits a clear plateau by day 6 and reaches half-maximal EdU+ CD8 SP development at day 3.5 and 4.5, respectively.
source: The percentage of EdU + CD8 SP thymocytes in OT-1 and F5 samples exhibits a clear plateau by day 6 and reaches half-maximal EdU + CD8 SP development at day 3.5 and 4.5, respectively.
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding based on the EdU data.

claim: The percentage of EdU+ CD8 SP thymocytes in TG6 samples continue to rise 9 days after the EdU pulse.
source: In contrast, the percentage of EdU + CD8 SP thymocytes in TG6 samples continue to rise 9 days after the EdU pulse (Figure 5c).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 5c.

claim: Increased time to complete positive selection is correlated with low self-reactivity in vivo.
source: This data shows that increased time to complete positive selection is also correlated with low self-reactivity in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript concludes this based on the EdU pulse data.

claim: Some CD8SP thymocytes of low self-reactivity can take longer than 7 days to complete positive selection.
source: Furthermore, these results show that some CD8SP thymocytes of low self-reactivity can take longer than 7 days to complete positive selection.
evidence: The manuscript concludes this based on the EdU pulse data showing continued rise at day 9.

claim: EdU+mature thymocytes found at earlier time points have higher CD5 compared to EdU+mature thymocytes found at later time points.
source: We observed that EdU+mature thymocytes found at earlier time points (and that therefore completed positive selection earlier) have higher CD5 compared to EdU +mature thymocytes found at later time points (Figure 5e,f).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 5e,f.

claim: The trend of lower CD5 at later time points is true for TCRβ+CD8 SP thymocytes and is even more dramatic in CD4SPs.
source: This is true for TCRβ+CD8 SP thymocytes; however, the trend is even more dramatic in CD4SPs (Figure 5f).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 5f.

claim: CD5 expression does not change with day post-EdU injection in TCR transgenic mice.
source: As expected, we did not observe changes in CD5 expression with day post-EdU injection in TCRtg mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The lower CD5 expression for polyclonal thymocytes completing positive selection at later time points reflects a shift in the repertoire toward TCRs with lower self-reactivity, rather than changes in maturation state.
source: This confirms that the lower CD5 expression for polyclonal thymocytes completing positive selection at later time points reflects a shift in the repertoire toward TCRs with lower self-reactivity, rather than changes in maturation state.
evidence: The manuscript infers this from the comparison of TCR transgenic and polyclonal data.

claim: Self-reactivity and time to complete positive selection are inversely correlated in nontransgenic mice for both MHC-I-restricted and MHC-II-restricted thymocytes.
source: These data indicate that self-reactivity and time to complete positive selection are also inversely correlated in nontransgenic mice, and this relationship exists for both MHC-I-restricted and MHC-II-restricted thymocytes.
evidence: The manuscript concludes this based on the polyclonal EdU data.

claim: Positive selection is accompanied by large-scale changes in gene expression.
source: Positive selection is accompanied by large-scale changes in gene expression, and delayed progress through positive selection for thymocytes with low self-reactivity might lead to synchronous or asynchronous delays in these gene expression changes.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge.

claim: TG6 and OT-1 thymocytes showed significant differences in gene expression at each developmental stage, with the number of differentially expressed genes decreasing with maturity.
source: TG6 and OT-1 thymocytes showed significant differences in gene expression at each developmental stage, with the number of differentially expressed genes decreasing with maturity (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Gene sets whose enrichment was associated with high self-reactivity (OT-1>F5>TG6) were related to ribosome function, RNA processing, and translation in early and late positive selection thymocytes.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed that gene sets whose enrichment was associated with high self-reactivity (i.e., OT-1 >F5>TG6) were related to ribosome function, RNA processing, and translation in early and late positive selection thymocytes (Figure 6a, top, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1, red dots).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 6a and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Genes involved in cell division and effector function were upregulated in mature CD8SP thymocytes with high self-reactivity.
source: Genes involved in cell division (Figure 6—figure supplement 1, purple dots) and effector function (Figure 6—figure supplement 1, blue dots) were also upregulated in mature CD8SP thymocytes with high self-reactivity (Figure 6a).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 6a and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Gene sets whose enrichment was associated with low self-reactivity (TG6>F5>OT-1) were related to transmembrane ion channel function, particularly voltage-gated ion channels.
source: Intriguingly, gene sets whose enrichment was associated with low self-reactivity (i.e., TG6 >F5>OT-1) were related to transmembrane ion channel function – particularly voltage-gated ion channels (Figure 6b, Figure 6—figure supplement 1, green dots).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 6b and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Leading-edge genes from ion channel-related gene sets included components of calcium (Cacna1e, Cacnb1, Cacnb3, Cacng4), potassium (Kcna2, Kcna3, Kcnh2, Kcnh3), sodium (Scn2b, Scn4b, Scn5a), and chloride (Clcn2) ion channels.
source: Genes contributing toward the enrichment scores of ion channel-related gene sets, or leading-edge genes, included components of calcium (Cacna1e, Cacnb1, Cacnb3, Cacng4), potassium (Kcna2, Kcna3, Kcnh2, Kcnh3), sodium (Scn2b, Scn4b, Scn5a), and chloride (Clcn2) ion channels.
evidence: The manuscript lists these genes as contributing to the enrichment scores.

claim: At all three developmental stages, there were more ion channel genes with higher gene expression in TG6 compared to OT-1 thymocytes.
source: At all three developmental stages, there were more ion channel genes with higher gene expression in TG6 (green bars) compared to OT-1 (red bars) thymocytes (Figure 6—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2a.

claim: Hierarchical clustering revealed a group of ion channel genes (group 2a) that shows a strong association with low self-reactivity and is also upregulated during early positive selection within each mouse strain.
source: Hierarchical clustering based on gene expression patterns across all samples revealed a group of genes (group 2a) that shows a strong association with low self-reactivity, and is also upregulated during early positive selection within each mouse strain.
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding based on hierarchical clustering analysis.

claim: Group 2a includes Scn4b, which encodes the regulatory subunit of a VGSC linked to positive selection.
source: This cluster includes Scn4b (Figure 6—figure supplement 2b), which encodes the regulatory subunit of a VGSC linked to positive selection (Lo et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript identifies Scn4b in this cluster and cites a study linking it to positive selection.

claim: Groups 1, 2b, and 3 of ion channel genes are upregulated in cells with low self-reactivity, but their expression peaks later during positive selection.
source: Groups 1, 2b, and 3 are also upregulated in cells with low self-reactivity, but their expression peaks later during positive selection.
evidence: The manuscript describes these groups based on the clustering analysis.

claim: Eleven of the 56 ion channel genes (group 4) have higher expression in cells with high self-reactivity and also peak at the mature CD8SP stage.
source: Eleven of the 56 genes (group 4) have higher expression in cells with high self-reactivity and also peak at the mature CD8SP stage.
evidence: The manuscript describes this group based on the clustering analysis.

claim: Group 4 includes P2rx7 and Trmp4, both of which have been linked to modulation of T cell effector responses.
source: This group includes P2r × 7 and Trmp4, both of which have been linked to modulation of T cell effector responses (Trebak and Kinet, 2019; Feske et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript identifies these genes in group 4 and cites studies linking them to T cell effector responses.

claim: Many ion channel genes whose expression correlated with low self-reactivity were also preferentially expressed at the early positive selection stage.
source: Many ion channel genes whose expression correlated with low self-reactivity were also preferentially expressed at the early positive selection stage (Figure 6c, group 2a), suggesting that thymocytes of low self-reactivity may retain an immature gene expression pattern later into positive selection.
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 6c and suggests an interpretation.

claim: Thymocytes of low self-reactivity may retain an immature gene expression pattern later into positive selection.
source: Many ion channel genes whose expression correlated with low self-reactivity were also preferentially expressed at the early positive selection stage (Figure 6c, group 2a), suggesting that thymocytes of low self-reactivity may retain an immature gene expression pattern later into positive selection.
evidence: The manuscript suggests this interpretation based on the gene expression data.

claim: A set of 11 genes was identified as a preselection DP gene signature using the dual criteria of high expression in CD69− DP and largest fold increase in CD69−DP relative to both DN4 and CD69+DP.
source: Specifically, we compared non-TCR transgenic, preselection (CD69−) DP thymocytes to their immediate progeny (CD69+) DP thymocytes, and to their immediate precursor (DN4 thymocytes), and identified a set of 11 genes using the dual criteria of high expression in CD69− DP, and largest fold increase in CD69−DP relative to both DN4 and CD69+DP (see Materials and methods) (Figure 6d, top, red dots).
evidence: The manuscript describes the method for identifying these genes with reference to Figure 6d.

claim: All 11 preselection DP signature genes correlated with low self-reactivity, particularly at the early DP stage of development.
source: Interestingly, all 11 genes correlated with low self-reactivity, particularly at the early DP stage of development.
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding based on the gene expression analysis.

claim: The preselection DP signature includes Themis, which encodes a protein required for modulating TCR signaling during positive selection.
source: This included Themis (Figure 6—figure supplement 2b), which encodes a protein required for modulating TCR signaling during positive selection (Lesourne et al., 2009; Patrick et al., 2009; Kakugawa et al., 2009; Fu et al., 2009; Johnson et al., 2009; Choi et al., 2017b; Choi et al., 2017a; Mehta et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript identifies Themis in the signature and cites multiple studies on its function.

claim: Expression of the curated set of ion channel genes in the ImmGen microarray data set revealed that group 2 genes displayed higher expression in preselection wild-type thymocytes.
source: Moreover, expression of the curated set of ion channel genes in the ImmGen microarray data set revealed that group 2 genes, whose expression correlated with low self-reactivity, also displayed higher expression in preselection wild-type thymocytes (Figure 6—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2c.

claim: GSEA between CD69− DP compared to DN4 or CD69+DP thymocytes showed enrichment of gene sets relating to ion channels.
source: Furthermore, GSEA between CD69− DP compared to DN4 or CD69+DP thymocytes showed enrichment of gene sets relating to ion channels (DN4<CD69 DP>CD69+DP) (Figure 6—figure supplement 2d).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2d.

claim: Cells with low self-reactivity retain a preselection DP phenotype later into development than those with high self-reactivity.
source: Together, this data suggests that cells with low self-reactivity retain a preselection DP phenotype later into development than those with high self-reactivity and that elevated expression of ion channel genes is a prominent feature of that phenotype.
evidence: The manuscript concludes this based on the gene expression data.

claim: Elevated expression of ion channel genes is a prominent feature of the preselection DP phenotype.
source: Together, this data suggests that cells with low self-reactivity retain a preselection DP phenotype later into development than those with high self-reactivity and that elevated expression of ion channel genes is a prominent feature of that phenotype.
evidence: The manuscript concludes this based on the gene expression data.

claim: There is another set of ion channel genes whose expression peaks at the late positive selection or CD8SP stage.
source: Retention of a preselection gene expression program can account for some, but not all, of the elevated ion channel gene expression by thymocytes of low self-reactivity. Specifically, there is another set of ion channel genes whose expression peaks at the late positive selection or CD8SP stage (Figure 6c, group 3).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 6c.

claim: Kcna2 and Tmie are upregulated in mature peripheral CD5 low CD8SP T cells relative to CD5 high CD8SP T cells.
source: Interestingly, two of these genes, Kcna2 and Tmie (Figure 6—figure supplement 2b), are also upregulated in mature peripheral CD5 low CD8SP T cells relative to CD5 high CD8SP T cells, based on published data sets (Supplementary files 3 and 4; Fulton et al., 2015; Matson et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2b and supplementary files, citing published data sets.

claim: Cells with low self-reactivity have high expression of the sodium-dependent neutral amino acid transporter Slc6a19.
source: Additionally, cells with low self-reactivity also have high expression of the sodium-dependent neutral amino acid transporter Slc6a19 (Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2b, Supplementary files 3 and 4; Fulton et al., 2015; Matson et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript presents this finding with reference to figures and supplementary files, citing published data sets.

claim: Elevated expression of distinct sets of ion channel genes is observed throughout the development of CD8 T cells with low self-reactivity.
source: Thus, elevated expression of distinct sets of ion channel genes is observed throughout the development of CD8 T cells with low self-reactivity.
evidence: The manuscript concludes this based on the gene expression data across developmental stages.

claim: Thymocytes with low self-reactivity experience briefer TCR signals and can take more than twice as long to complete positive selection, compared to those with relatively high self-reactivity.
source: Here we show that thymocytes with low self-reactivity experience briefer TCR signals and can take more than twice as long to complete positive selection, compared to those with relatively high self-reactivity.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes this as a main finding in the Discussion.

claim: Thymocytes with low self-reactivity retain a preselection gene expression program as they progress through development, including elevated expression of genes previously implicated in modulating TCR signaling during positive selection and a novel set of ion channel genes.
source: Thymocytes with low self-reactivity retain a preselection gene expression program as they progress through development, including elevated expression of genes previously implicated in modulating TCR signaling during positive selection, and a novel set of ion channel genes.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes this as a main finding in the Discussion.

claim: A separate set of ion channel genes that peaks at the CD8SP stage is also selectively upregulated in mature CD8SP thymocytes of low self-reactivity.
source: In addition, a separate set of ion channel genes that peaks at the CD8SP stage is also selectively upregulated in mature CD8SP thymocytes of low self-reactivity.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes this as a main finding in the Discussion.

claim: The modulation of TCR sensitivity during T cell development occurs with distinct kinetics for T cells with low self-reactivity.
source: These results indicate that the modulation of TCR sensitivity during T cell development occurs with distinct kinetics for T cells with low self-reactivity and associates membrane ion channel expression with early and late stages of T cell development as well as T cell self-reactivity.
evidence: The manuscript concludes this based on the overall findings.

claim: Membrane ion channel expression is associated with early and late stages of T cell development as well as T cell self-reactivity.
